title: Sand Separator
model_title: Sand Separator — Inclined Screw Classifier (Coarse Sand from Red Mud Slurry)

introduction.definition: A sand separator removes coarse sand from red mud slurry. In an inclined screw classifier, sand settles in a pool and a slowly turning screw rakes it up the incline, draining it, while fine mud overflows to the washers.
applications: Sand removal in Bayer residue circuits
introduction.summary: A sand separator removes coarse sand from the red mud slurry. In an inclined screw classifier the sand settles in a pool and is raked up the incline by a slowly turning screw, draining as it goes, while fine mud overflows to the washers.

pressure.title: Sand settles, mud overflows
pressure.description: Coarse sand (typically > ~ 100 µm) settles quickly in the pool and is raked up the incline, draining and being washed on the way, while fine red mud stays in suspension and overflows the weir to the washers. Removing sand early reduces erosion in thickeners, pumps and pipelines; the washed sand is often used for residue-area construction.

video_tutorials.title: Sand Separator — Introduction

script.narration: This module introduces the Sand Separator.
A sand separator removes coarse sand from red mud slurry.
In an inclined screw classifier, sand settles in a pool and a slowly turning screw rakes it up the incline, draining it, while fine mud overflows to the washers.
Typical applications include sand removal in Bayer residue circuits; mineral sand classification.
The cutaway reveals the internal construction: Inclined Trough & Settling Pool (with overflow weir), Spiral Screw (rakes settled sand up the incline).
The exploded view separates every component so each one can be tapped for its function, material and failure modes.
Next, watch the operation tutorial to see how it works.

script.narration: How the Sand Separator works.
Slurry enters the pool.
Sand settles; fines stay suspended.
The screw rakes sand up the incline.
Sand discharges at the top.
The flow overlay traces the liquid from suction to discharge.

Coarse sand (typically > ~ 100 µm) settles quickly in the pool and is raked up the incline, draining and being washed on the way, while fine red mud stays in suspension and overflows the weir to the washers.

script.narration: Maintenance essentials for the Sand Separator.
Check sand moisture and screw.
Inspect wear shoes.
Replace flights.
Watch for screw overload: trip. Common cause: sand surge.
Watch for fines in sand: wet, muddy sand. Common cause: high feed rate.
Record every inspection so trends — vibration, temperature, leakage and performance — can be compared over time.
